title: Tangent Mirror basis with nonlinear private residual
hypothesis: A shared rank-2 tangent basis with task Mirror coordinates will fit small, approximately linearizable adaptations using fewer bytes than private full updates. For tasks with a large nonlinear residual, adding a private rank-1 nonlinear weight residual should recover query quality with less state than a full per-task update. Stratify fresh tasks by their known teacher residual amplitude before averaging.
physical_object: shared base tanh network and rank-2 tangent basis over output-weight perturbations
mirror_coordinate: task coefficients in shared first-order Jacobian basis
logical_multiplicity: multiple task-specific local adaptations around one shared base
controls: first-order tangent model with task code only
tangent code plus task-private rank-1 nonlinear residual (LoRA-shaped control)
linearized tuning with an equivalent rank-1 residual
task: Synthetic vector regression with shared tanh base, low-rank task tangent directions, and a preregistered easy/hard residual stratum; report query MSE by stratum and actual serialized bytes.

development.selection_metric: query MSE by residual stratum, byte frontier and private-state activation rate; no fresh tuning

fresh.split: 4 development task IDs for fixed tangent basis setup; each fresh world has 4 low-residual and 4 high-residual task IDs, 32 support and 256 query examples per task

success_gate: On >=2/3 fresh seeds, low-residual tangent Mirror MSE <= 1e-2 and uses <=60% full-update payload. On high-residual tasks, private rank-1 residual reduces query MSE by >=50% vs tangent-only while hybrid payload <=70% full-update payload.
failure_gate: FAIL if either stratum misses its quality/storage gate on >=2/3 seeds, or private residual does not improve high-residual quality; PROMISING only if low-residual gate passes and high-residual private residual is useful but misses a byte gate narrowly.
boundaries: task teacher shares a known tangent subspace
no capacity claim from fixed updates
private residual threshold does not generalize without non-synthetic task families
